_link.title: I can explain sprouting as a mechanism of synaptic plasticity

toLevel2.stem: What is sprouting in the context of synaptic plasticity?
toLevel2.answer: The growth of new dendritic or axonal branches
distractors: The removal of unused synaptic connections
The redirection of signals to new pathways
The strengthening of existing receptor sites

toLevel2.stem: Which structures are involved in sprouting?
distractors: Synaptic vesicles only
Receptor sites and ions
Myelin sheaths and nodes

toLevel2.stem: What does sprouting enable a neuron to do?
distractors: Increase its firing threshold
Reduce its chemical output
Replace its damaged cell body

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting is classified as which type of change in the nervous system?
distractors: A chemical change only
An electrical change only
A temporary functional shift

toLevel2.stem: Which of the following best describes the result of sprouting?
toLevel2.answer: Increased reach and new neural connections
distractors: Decreased neural activity and fewer links
Faster transmission within existing paths
Removal of inactive dendritic extensions

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting involves the development of new extensions or branches from dendrites or axons.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting refers to the elimination of unused synaptic connections between neurons.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting is the ability of dendrites or axons to develop new {{blank:1}} or branches.

distractors: receptors
vesicles

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting increases the {{blank:1}} of a neuron and enables the formation of new synaptic connections.

distractors: speed
charge

toLevel2.stem: Sprouting is one of the three mechanisms of {{blank:1}}, alongside rerouting and pruning.

distractors: synaptic transmission
receptor specificity

toLevel3.stem: How does sprouting contribute to the process of learning a new skill?
toLevel3.answer: It creates new connections between neurons
distractors: It removes connections that are not needed
It speeds up existing electrical impulses
It reduces the number of active synapses

toLevel3.stem: Why is sprouting considered a structural change rather than a purely chemical change?
toLevel3.answer: It involves physical growth of neural branches
distractors: It alters the type of neurotransmitter released
It changes the electrical charge of the neuron
It increases the concentration of neurochemicals

toLevel3.stem: Which statement best explains how sprouting differs from rerouting?
toLevel3.answer: Sprouting grows new branches; rerouting redirects signals
distractors: Sprouting removes connections; rerouting creates new ones
Sprouting is temporary; rerouting is a permanent change
Sprouting occurs in the CNS; rerouting occurs in the PNS

toLevel3.stem: In what way does sprouting support recovery from brain injury?
toLevel3.answer: New branches form connections around damaged areas
distractors: Damaged neurons regenerate their original cell body
Existing connections become stronger automatically
The brain reduces its overall neural activity level

toLevel3.stem: Why is sprouting listed as a structural change associated with long-term potentiation?
toLevel3.answer: It physically expands neural pathway connections
distractors: It temporarily increases neurotransmitter release
It reduces the threshold for an action potential
It changes receptor sensitivity without new growth

toLevel3.stem: How does sprouting increase the capacity of a neural pathway?
toLevel3.answer: By adding new connections to neighbouring neurons
distractors: By widening the synaptic cleft between neurons
By increasing the size of the neuronal cell body
By thickening the myelin sheath on existing axons

toLevel3.stem: Sprouting supports learning by enabling the formation of new synaptic connections in brain regions associated with the skill being learned.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Sprouting supports learning because new dendritic branches allow neurons to form {{blank:1}} with other neurons.

distractors: stronger charges
faster impulses

toLevel3.stem: Unlike pruning, which removes unused connections, sprouting {{blank:1}} the number of synaptic connections.

distractors: decreases
maintains

toLevel3.stem: Sprouting is associated with long-term potentiation because it represents a {{blank:1}} change that strengthens neural pathways.

distractors: temporary
electrical

toLevel4.stem: Tara begins learning to play the violin. Which example best illustrates how sprouting would occur in her brain?
toLevel4.answer: Dendrites grow new branches in motor cortex regions
distractors: Unused visual processing connections are removed
Existing auditory neurons fire more frequently
Neurotransmitter levels increase across her brain

toLevel4.stem: After a stroke damages part of Raj's left hemisphere, he gradually recovers some language ability. Which application of sprouting best explains this recovery?
toLevel4.answer: Neurons near the damage grew new branches to form connections
distractors: The damaged neurons fully regenerated their original structure
Raj's right hemisphere was always responsible for his language
Neurotransmitter levels increased to compensate for the damage

toLevel4.stem: Mia practises a new dance routine daily for several weeks. Which observation would best indicate that sprouting has occurred?
toLevel4.answer: Increased dendritic branching in relevant brain areas
distractors: Faster reuptake of neurotransmitters after practice
Reduced number of synapses in her motor regions
Higher concentration of GABA across her whole brain

toLevel4.stem: A neuroscientist examines brain tissue from a person who spent years learning multiple languages. Which finding would be most consistent with sprouting?
toLevel4.answer: Greater dendritic density in language-related regions
distractors: Fewer neural connections in language-related areas
Thinner myelin sheaths on all cortical axon fibres
Reduced receptor sites across the temporal lobe area

toLevel4.stem: Jake has not practised guitar for several years and notices his skills have declined. If sprouting contributed to his original skill development, which process most likely accounts for the decline?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning of the connections that sprouting created
distractors: Further sprouting in unrelated brain regions only
Rerouting of signals away from his motor regions
Increased sprouting that overwhelmed his pathways

toLevel4.stem: Dr Patel is studying brain plasticity in patients undergoing rehabilitation after a head injury. She observes new dendritic growth near the injury site. Which mechanism of synaptic plasticity does this observation illustrate?
distractors: Pruning
Rerouting
Potentiation

toLevel4.stem: Lily is told that her intensive study schedule is causing structural changes in her brain. Which scenario best represents sprouting as a result of her studying?
toLevel4.answer: New dendritic branches form in areas she is using
distractors: Unused synaptic connections are being eliminated
Neural signals are being rerouted to new regions
Her neurons are producing a different neurotransmitter

toLevel4.stem: When Amir learns to type, sprouting would involve the growth of new {{blank:1}} in the brain regions responsible for fine motor control.

distractors: synaptic vesicles
receptor proteins

toLevel4.stem: A patient recovering from brain injury shows new neural growth near the damaged area. This is an example of {{blank:1}} supporting the formation of {{blank:2}}.

distractors: pruning
rerouting
new cell bodies
stronger charges

toLevel4.stem: If a musician practises daily for months, sprouting would be expected to {{blank:1}} the number of synaptic connections in the relevant brain regions.

distractors: decrease
maintain

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that sprouting alone is sufficient to explain all learning and memory in the brain. Which evaluation of this claim is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; learning also involves rerouting and pruning
distractors: Correct; sprouting is the only structural change needed
Correct; other mechanisms are only relevant to injury
Incorrect; sprouting does not contribute to any learning

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee argues that sprouting is more important than pruning for effective learning. Which evaluation best addresses this claim?
toLevel5.answer: Both are essential; new connections and removal of old ones work together
distractors: Correct; pruning only occurs during brain injury recovery and not learning
Correct; sprouting is the only mechanism that creates lasting neural change
Incorrect; pruning is the sole mechanism responsible for all memory formation

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that sprouting cannot occur in adult brains because neural development is complete by adolescence. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sprouting occurs throughout life in response to experience
distractors: Correct; only children's brains are capable of structural changes
Correct; adult brains rely solely on chemical changes for learning
Incorrect; sprouting only occurs during prenatal brain development

toLevel5.stem: Emma suggests that if sprouting occurs during learning, then more practice should always lead to more dendritic branches without limit. Which evaluation is most accurate?
distractors: Correct; there is no limit to dendritic branching
Correct; practice always produces more new branches
Incorrect; practice has no effect on neural growth

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that sprouting during recovery from brain injury produces connections identical to the original ones. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Unlikely; new connections may differ from original pathways
distractors: Correct; sprouting always replicates the original network
Correct; the brain's blueprint ensures identical regrowth
Incorrect; sprouting cannot occur after any brain injury

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that sprouting is a chemical change because it involves neurotransmitters. Which evaluation of this classification is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sprouting is a structural change involving physical growth
distractors: Correct; all synaptic plasticity is classified as chemical change
Correct; the involvement of neurotransmitters makes it a chemical change
Incorrect; sprouting is an electrical change rather than structural change

toLevel5.stem: Tom argues that sprouting in response to learning a new language would only occur in Broca's area. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; multiple brain regions would show sprouting
distractors: Correct; language learning only involves one brain region
Correct; Broca's area is the only region capable of change
Incorrect; sprouting cannot occur in Broca's area at all

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that sprouting and long-term potentiation are the same process. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sprouting is one structural change within LTP
distractors: Correct; the two terms are interchangeable in psychology
Correct; both refer to the same growth of neural branches
Incorrect; sprouting and LTP are entirely unrelated concepts

toLevel5.stem: The claim that sprouting alone explains all learning is {{blank:1}} because effective learning also requires {{blank:2}} and rerouting.

distractors: correct
plausible
myelination
inhibition

toLevel5.stem: Sprouting is correctly classified as a {{blank:1}} change rather than a chemical change because it involves the physical growth of new neural branches.

distractors: chemical
electrical
